Subject: Reopen: Order form & packaging split – request for fallback language

Hi Sean / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement team reviewed the draft order form and we'd like to reopen the pricing exhibit to add a more explicit tier-fallback mechanism and a one-time packaging split for our Q1 onboarding. The attached files are the draft order form and our annotated redlines (Acme_Orderform_Draft_v3.pdf, Acme_redlines_v3.docx).

Key asks from our side:
- A temporary reduction of the minimum floor for first 3 months while we ramp usage
- An explicit fallback to the prior tiered rates if commit thresholds are not met
- A carveout for a one-off packaging split so different product bundles map to different fee bands for the pilot

Can you confirm if Redwood can accept a temporary floor adjustment and outline what the fallback trigger would look like in the order schedule? We are trying to finalize the commercial terms this month.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Procurement – Acme Cloud Ltd

Marta — thanks for the note and attachments. We can discuss the temporary floor adjustment; we want to avoid an open-ended rollback that creates downstream billing ambiguity.

Initial thoughts from commercial:
- We can put a 90-day ramp floor at X% of the stated minimum, after which the standard minimum resumes unless a documented remediation plan is in place.
- Fallback should be milestone-driven (e.g., 60/90/180 day checkpoints) rather than purely usage-triggered to avoid measurement disputes.
- Packaging split looks doable for a one-time mapping change in the order schedule, but we need a clear SKU-to-band mapping and a sunset date.

I'm attaching a short matrix we use internally for fallback scenarios (proposed-fallback-matrix.xlsx). Laura — can you take the lead on a legal redline for Exhibit B and the order schedule?

Happy to hop on a call tomorrow afternoon to run through the examples.

—Sean

Sean — quick follow up from procurement. Two specific items we need reflected in the order schedule:

1) A Q1 pilot floor set at 50% of the annual minimum for the first 90 days (retroactive true-up at end of Q1).
2) A fallback that reverts to the previous effective tiered rate card if average monthly tokens over a 60-day window fall below the stated commit by more than 40% — we need clear measurement windows and service-to-bill mapping.

We can send a sample SKU mapping for the packaging split by EOD. Also, we will need a DocuSign envelope for an amendment once we lock wording. Can you confirm your legal and finance teams can sign a short amendment?

Thanks,
Procurement Team
Acme Cloud Ltd
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Date: 2026-12-11T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Reopen: Order form & packaging split – request for fallback language

Marta / Team — attaching a markup of the Order Schedule and Exhibit B (OrderSchedule_Markup.pdf). A few legal points and proposed language below. Please treat these as redlines for discussion, not final: 

Highlights / concerns:
- Open-ended ramps: we will not accept an indefinite floor reduction. Proposed wording: "Temporary Floor Adjustment": the parties agree to a temporary reduction of the Minimum Commitment to 50% of the Annual Minimum for a period of ninety (90) days commencing on the Effective Date of the Amendment; notwithstanding the foregoing, if at the ninety-day checkpoint Customer has not met the agreed milestone (defined below), Customer shall revert to the Annual Minimum and be subject to a true-up pro rata for the shortfall.

- Measurement windows: move to a 60-day rolling average for usage measurement, with a 7-day cure period for measurement disputes. This avoids reactive billing changes for anomalous spikes/dips.

- Fallback trigger mechanics: remove any clause that permits unilateral reversion to “prior tiered rates” without clear prior period references. Proposed fix: an explicit matrix in Exhibit B that maps SKU groups to prior effective rate bands and defines the temporal window (preceding 6 months average) used to calculate the fallback rate.

- Packaging split: accept a one-time mapping for pilot bundles provided the mapping is enumerated in Annex A and the mapping expires after 120 days, unless extended by written amendment.

- Revenue protection carveouts: Legal is open to limited concessions (temporary floors) only if accompanied by a staged recovery plan and a cap on the number of consecutive quarters with reduced floors.

Next steps:
1) If Acme provides the SKU mapping we will incorporate it directly into Annex A and prepare a clean amendment + DocuSign envelope for signature.
2) If you prefer, we can run a short working session to align the fallback matrix and milestone definitions.

Quoted for context:
> "Two specific items we need reflected in the order schedule: A Q1 pilot floor set at 50%..."

Attachments: OrderSchedule_Markup.pdf (application/pdf)

—Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Marta — appreciate the quick responses and for sending the SKU mapping earlier today. Summary / proposed operational pathway so we can close this week:

1) Redwood accepts a 90-day temporary floor at 50% with a pro rata true-up at the end of the pilot as described by Laura.
2) Fallback will be governed by an explicit matrix in Exhibit B that references the prior six months’ effective rates; measurement will be a 60-day rolling average with a 7-day dispute cure window.
3) Packaging split will be recorded as a one-time Annex A mapping that expires after 120 days unless mutually extended.
4) Legal to prepare a clean amendment incorporating the redlines. We propose a short DocuSign envelope for signature targeted for EOD Friday.

If that aligns, I'll schedule a 2:00pm PT working call Thursday to walk through the matrix with your team and our finance/ops folks. HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2026-117
DocuSign: https://docusign.net/link/ABC123efg

Thanks — looking forward to closing.
—Sean
